title: What If a Magnitude 10 Earthquake Hit?

scenes.text: What if a magnitude 10 earthquake hit? The twist is, it can't.
The biggest ever recorded was 9.5, in Chile in 1960. It broke a fault nearly 1,000 miles long.
Magnitude depends on how much fault slips, and a bigger quake needs a longer fault.
A magnitude 10 would need a fault stretching around most of the planet.
No fault that long is known to exist, according to the USGS.
So the biggest quake humans will ever face is about a 9.5. That one already shook the whole Pacific.

description:
What if a magnitude 10 earthquake hit?
According to the USGS, it can't happen. A fault long enough would have to wrap most of the way around the planet.
